Daniel Defoe, Moll Flanders.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/daniel-defoe/moll-flanders

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Daniel Defoe, the author, died 1731.

First publication of the text used: 1722 (SE colophon: 'was published in 1722 by Daniel Defoe'). Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moll_Flanders) gives 1722, publisher William Rufus Chetwood, and country Kingdom of Great Britain.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1722, before 1923, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (Kingdom of Great Britain, the United Kingdom's predecessor state): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last person named above. The last to die did so in 1731, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 1802.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
